text:
alex: Heads up — I'm seeing org-level spikes that exhaust per-key tokens in ~10s, then a long tail of 429s. Think we need a different burst strategy than the current token_bucket. Thoughts?

maria: Can you paste an example trace and the token settings you saw?

alex: Trace: rapid ~2k reqs in 8s from same org. Current config: `rate=50/s, burst=500`. System drops requests when KV cache cold and latency spikes.

devang: Token bucket lets big bursts through if you have a large bucket. Leaky bucket smooths the output but introduces queueing/backpressure. For short spikes leaky can keep CPU steady but may increase client latency.

tess: We need to keep console UX simple. Right now we show a single "burst" slider. If we add a `smoothing_window` param folks will be confused. Suggest opt-in beta behind advanced toggle with a short description.

alex: Proposed hybrid idea: keep token_bucket by default but add a small short-window cap so you can't exhaust everything instantly. Eg: `burst=500, rate=50, short_cap=300/5s` — tokens still refill but you can only consume 300 requests per 5s window.

maria: Short_cap seems promising — gives predictable tail behavior. We'll need telemetry: per-key `burst_consumed` counter + rolling 10s consumption histogram. Expose these in the console and wire alerts for unusual short-window utilization.

devang: Implementation note: do this in request router middleware. Maintain sliding window counters per key + token bucket fallback. Use approximate counters (fixed N buckets) to keep memory cheap. Pseudocode: ```if (sliding_window_count(key, 5s) >= short_cap) reject; else try_token_bucket();```

alex: Rollout plan: canary to 5% of orgs with the highest traffic for 24h. Compare 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, and rejected-by-short-cap counts.
tess: UI: on rollout page show "expected rejections" calc and a knob "allow higher short bursts" for enterprise customers with a note about latency/cost tradeoffs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started canary deploy for `burst-smoothing-params` -> 5% groups. (link: https://deploys/redwood/canary/345)

jon: Also: keep quotas API backward compatible. When rejecting include `x-quota-reason: short_cap` or `x-quota-reason: burst` so clients can differentiate. Add a human-friendly explanation in the response body.

sam: :thumbsup: make sure SLO owners get a chart of p95/p99 lat vs token consumption and a heatmap of short-window rejections by org.

alex: I'll draft an RFC with config schema, metric names, and console mock. Will ping eng-sre for alert thresholds and eng-telemetry for dashboards.
